newsitem.title: INDIA: British Airways link with India airline.
newsitem.headline: British Airways link with India airline.

text.p: British Airways (BA) said on Thursday it had entered a marketing partnership in frequent flyer programmes with an Indian private airline, Jet Airways.

Under the partnership, Indian residents who belong to BA's Executive Club programme can get credits for free travel across India on Jet Airways. Jet's Privilege Programme customers can get similar benefits for international travel with BA, the British airline said in a statement.
The partnership would take effect from November, BA said.

"The new partnership does not involve exchange of equity or other forms of cross-shareholding. British Airways and Jet Airways remain separate entities, retaining their own identities and brands," the statement said.

Officials from both airlines said there was no financial exchange involved in the agreement, which also does not form any exclusive arrangement that would bar marketing partnerships with other airlines.
But they said the partnership with Jet Airways could be upgraded sometime in the future.

"Of course, we have plans," Kevin Steele, British Airways' general manager for South Asia, told a news conference, but added that their outcome would depend on further talks between the two airlines and approval from the Indian government.
"We are very cost conscious. And we are looking at a long-term relationship," said Naresh Goyal, chairman of Jet Airways.

Steele said the partnership augured well for British Airways because India's internal air traffic was growing at an annual rate of between 10 and 15 percent while West-bound travel from India was growing at a rate of 10 to 12 percent.
"I am extremely bullish about what's happening in India," Steele said.
